Recipe: Bark armor (Level 1). You have seen bark armor. Plates of bark laced together, worn like a shell.

🛡️ Dawn at Haven. By the fire hangs an old bark cuirass, split at the seam — somebody's grandfather wore this into the treeline and came back. The shape of it is clear: bark plates laced overlapping like shingles, vine cord. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
Rain. Steady, cold, honest rain.
⚠ STARVING: health and energy falling. You went to bed on an empty stomach.

A woman, maybe 60s is staring into the fire like it owes them answers.
A person, maybe 40s, with a wiry build came back with 539 kcal of something edible. The pantry breathes.

Travel 1 tile to trail edge.
— An old trail —
A game trail crosses your path — two toes, heart-shaped, heading for water.
Something big is moving in the woods. The birds went quiet.
Movement — a long gray snake coiled on a sunlit log.
👁 No rattle, no venom — but your hands don't know that yet. It freezes, hoping you'll walk past. Pin it behind the head; it bites only when grabbed.
You catch fragments by the fire — A woman, maybe 60s telling Eduardo about you. Half of it's true anymore. You're not sure which half.

You catch fragments by the fire — Chantal telling Mia about you. The details have shifted. Nobody seems to mind.
This patch is worked out — step to another green patch and forage again.

Travel 2 tiles to forest floor.
— Under the canopy —
Saplings push up through last year's deadfall, racing each other for the light. The forest never stops trying.
Something moves out there — two knobs on glass-still water, watching.
Movement — a great horned owl, silent and huge.
👁 It waits for YOU to come close — the stillness is the trap. Spot the shape before you're in reach, and strike first. It only gets one.
You see smoke on the horizon. Thornfield — 11 people, 3 days in. fishing folk, by the look of it. They know 2 plants — 2 new to you. They've been here the whole time.
This patch is worked out — step to another green patch and forage again.

Travel 1 tile to Haven.
The raccoon with too many fingers stops at the treeline — pacing, unwilling. The walls end the argument. It's still out there.
2 unprocessed hauls onto the counter — the clock is ticking.
Someone by the fire nods at the counter. "We pool food here. Keep what you need for the road — the rest feeds everyone, once it's food."
Nobody at the fire knows your haul any better than you do. It'll be your own hands that teach you.

★ IDENTIFIED: Mahua. The flowers fall like rain and taste like brown sugar — then they ferment. Uses unknown — harvest, taste, and learn.
You were listening. Now you know Mahua too.
